conflict_synopsis.core_view: BoC is the laggard: energy pass-through plus still-firm Canadian demand make CA 5Y too rich versus a Fed that has already hiked, so CA-US 5Y should rise from a 0th-percentile -124bp extreme.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: BoC confirmation that fuel inflation is passing through, against policy still at 2.25%.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: BoC treats labor cooling and on-target core as binding and leaves the Canada discount to US 5Y in place.

remit: underpriced hawkish policy, higher terminal rates, or higher-rate repricing
stance_summary: Verified: the Fed has already hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% into a >90% priced decision, US 5Y is 4.86% near the top of its one-year distribution, while the BoC is still holding 2.25% with CA 5Y at 3.54%. The common-date CA-US 5Y spread is -124bp, 0th percentile, z about -2.05, and cheapened about 12bp over five sessions as US yields rose and Canadian yields fell. Inference: that gap is the underpriced hawk, not another outright pay of already-extreme US duration. BoC minutes flag energy pass-through as the conditional tightening trigger, Brent is 130.8 (99.6th percentile) and WTI 107.02, Canada headline CPI is still 3.0% against policy at 2.25%, and CA activity/consumer temperatures (53.2 / 52.5) plus Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q show demand has not collapsed. Unknown: no BoC OIS path is in the packet; core trim/median are already near 2%; August employment -42k, unemployment 6.4%, and wages +2.0% y/y are genuine labor cooling. The trade is therefore relative: pay Canada 5Y versus receive US 5Y so that a BoC catch-up, not a global duration squeeze, owns the discrepancy.

catalysts: Next BoC deliberations or speakers confirming that fuel inflation is spreading into broader CPI.
Canadian CPI prints that lift headline further above 3% or push trim/median off the 2% handle.
Persistence of Brent/WTI near the packet extremes, keeping the pass-through trigger live.
Continued G10 tightening impulse (post-Fed, post-BoJ, hawkish BoE minority) that forces laggard CBs to reprice.
trade.direction: long CA-US 5Y spread (pay CA 5Y / receive US 5Y)
evidence_refs: rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk
rollup:Canada August inflation holds at 3%, core stays near 2%
rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Long CA-US 5Y spread: pay CA 5Y versus receive US 5Y (Canada rates catch up to the post-hike US path).
expression_comparison.rationale: The discrepancy is a cross-market policy-path gap, not a CAD-beta gap. CA-US 5Y is a clean, executable-from-packet 5Y RV at a 0th-percentile common-date extreme after a 5D cheapening. Short USDCAD is inferior: the packet's USDCAD vs CA-US 2Y screen is weak (r-squared about 0.022), USDCAD already sits at the 87th percentile with a 1m rise of about 1.74%, the 2Y differential of 140bp favors long USD versus CAD so spot fights carry, and high oil is a Canada-exporter CAD tail that contaminates a pure hawk expression. Rates are preferred when comparably clean; here they are cleaner.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short USDCAD (CAD higher if BoC tightening is repriced).

trade.horizon: 4-12 weeks, into the next BoC communication cycle on energy pass-through
trade.invalidation: BoC communication that energy pass-through will not trigger tightening, or a Canadian data sequence in which core stays at or below 2% while labor keeps deteriorating, such that the CA-US 5Y catch-up thesis is abandoned even if the spread remains historically negative. A US-only further squeeze that cheapens CA-US 5Y without any BoC reaction-function shift also falsifies the relative expression.
trade.mispricing: Market pricing embeds a 124bp 5Y Canada discount to the United States at the 0th percentile of the 252-observation common-date sample after a 5D CA-US 5Y move of -12bp (z about -2.03). That is the opposite of a BoC that has just told markets energy pass-through risk has increased. US front-end and 5Y yields already sit at the 99th-100th percentile after a fully priced 25bp hike; Canada has not repriced the same global tightening impulse.
principal_risks: Canada labor is already weak (unemployment 6.4%, employment -42k, wages +2.0% y/y); BoC may treat that as binding and stay on hold.
CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0% are at target; if energy stays in headline only, the reaction-function trigger never fires.
Receiving US 5Y loses if the Fed keeps hiking faster than BoC catch-up; US 5Y is already at the 99.6th percentile.
Saudi workaround and any further oil easing can remove the pass-through catalyst.
No positioning, OIS, or executable broker prices are in the packet; snapshot CA (17 Sep) and US (18 Sep) as-of dates differ except on the common-date spread.
AU housing stress and NZ rate unavailability are not used; they do not rescue a Canada-specific miss.
trade.structure: Matched 5Y cross-market RV: pay CA 5Y / receive US 5Y using official research/reference sovereign yields; not broker-executable.
trade.thesis: Causal question: is the BoC still treating the energy shock as containable while the Fed, BoJ and a hawkish minority of global peers have already tightened, so that Canadian 5Y yields remain too low versus US 5Y? Verified state: Fed funds 3.75-4.00% after a 25bp hike; BoC 2.25% hold; CA-US 5Y -124bp on 2026-09-17, percentile 0.0, z -2.05; CA 5Y 3.54% fell about 9bp over five sessions while US 5Y 4.86% rose about 8bp. Verified composition: Canada headline CPI held at 3.0% y/y, CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0%; activity temperature 53.2 with real GDP +0.8% q/q and strong retail; consumer temperature 52.5. Transmission: xa:energy-retained and BoC minutes identify broader fuel pass-through as the clearest conditional trigger for renewed tightening; Brent 130.8 and WTI 107.02 keep that channel live even after a Saudi workaround reduced the extreme supply tail. Pricing already requires a large Canada discount to the US: US 2Y 4.76% is at the 100th percentile of the stretched screen, so another outright pay of US duration is chasing a completed hike, whereas CA 5Y 5y-z is only about 0.81. Inference: the closing mechanism is BoC reaction-function catch-up into energy persistence and still-firm demand, lifting CA 5Y more than US 5Y and raising the CA-US 5Y spread from a historically extreme negative. Unknowns that cut the size: August CA labor is clearly weaker (employment -42k, unemployment 6.4%, wages +2.0% y/y), core is near target, no hike-probability strip is supplied, and positioning is unavailable.
why_now: Fed hike on 16 Sep 2026 to 3.75-4.00% is now in the price (>90% pre-decision), while CA 5Y still sold off about 9bp over five sessions and the CA-US 5Y spread printed a 0th-percentile extreme.
BoC minutes retained in xa:energy-retained explicitly raise fuel-inflation pass-through risk as the conditional tightening trigger against policy still at 2.25%.
Desk thesis on 18 Sep 2026: global tightening is broadening (BoJ to 1.25%, BoE 6-3 hold with three hike votes and gilt QT), keeping term-rate pressure elevated even where domestic growth is softer.
Brent 130.8 (99.6th percentile) and WTI 107.02 keep the energy channel live; Canada headline inflation remains 3.0% versus a 2.25% policy rate.
